issues.legal_issue: A quasi-judicial authority’s deliberate and mala fide refusal to follow a binding High Court precedent, on improper grounds, constitutes contempt of court.
material_facts: A quasi-judicial authority deciding a revision was subject to the High Court’s superintendence.
The High Court had decided the identical legal issue and its decision was cited to the authority.
The authority declined to follow that decision, stating that the matter was before the Supreme Court, although only a petition for a certificate to appeal was pending in the High Court.
The authority used language identifying itself with a litigant and relied on factually wrong and illegitimate reasons to avoid the precedent.
The High Court found the conduct mala fide and held the authority guilty of contempt; the authority appealed.
issues.conclusion: The deliberate and mala fide refusal to follow the binding High Court decision constituted contempt. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and upheld the contempt finding.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 227 of the Constitution, decisions of a High Court bind courts and tribunals subject to its superintendence, including a quasi-judicial authority. Deliberate, mala fide non-compliance with such a precedent can undermine the High Court’s authority and the administration of law and therefore fall within contempt; a bona fide but mistaken distinguishing of a binding precedent does not. The Court relied on the principles of contempt, including willful disregard of judicial authority and conduct bringing the administration of law into disrepute, and on East India Commercial Co. Ltd. v. Collector of Customs, Calcutta, [1963] 3 S.C.R. 338; Article 215 was also discussed in the cited reasoning.

rule.if: appeal_from_contempt_finding and quasi_judicial_authority and subject_to_high_court_superintendence and binding_high_court_precedent and precedent_not_followed and deliberate_bad_faith_avoidance

predicates.appeal_from_contempt_finding: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a finding that an authority committed contempt.
predicates.quasi_judicial_authority: The person who did not follow the precedent was acting as a quasi-judicial authority.
predicates.subject_to_high_court_superintendence: The authority was subject to the supervisory jurisdiction of the High Court whose precedent it did not follow.
predicates.binding_high_court_precedent: The High Court had already decided the same legal issue, and its decision bound the authority.
predicates.precedent_not_followed: The authority decided the matter without following the applicable High Court decision.
predicates.deliberate_bad_faith_avoidance: The authority deliberately avoided the precedent in bad faith by relying on wrong or illegitimate reasons.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a contempt finding against a quasi-judicial authority subject to High Court superintendence, and that authority deliberately avoids a binding High Court precedent in bad faith, the rule treats the authority as having committed contempt.
